abstract: We show that, for every fixed proper minor-closed graph class $\mathcal{G}$ and every positive integer $n$, there exists a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1+o(1)}$ vertices and edges such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $U_n$. This result generalizes and unifies the results of Dujmovi\'c et al. (J. ACM 2021) on induced-universal graphs and the results of Esperet, Joret, and Morin (J. London Math. Soc. 2023) on sparse induced-universal graphs from planar graphs to all proper minor-closed graph classes. It simultaneously improves the previous bounds for the number of vertices in induced-universal graphs (previously $O(n^2)$ obtained as a corollary of a result of DeVos et al. (J. Comb. Theory, Ser. {B} 2004) and a result of Gavoille and Labourel (ESA 2007)) and the number of edges in subgraph-universal graphs (previously $O(n^{3/2})$ by Babai et al. (Theory and Practice of Combinatorics 1982)).
hook: Graphs from any minor-closed class fit inside one sparse graph with only n^(1+o(1)) vertices and edges.
hook_turn: with only n^(1+o(1)) vertices and edges.
summary: For any proper minor-closed class, such as planar graphs, the authors construct a graph that contains every n-vertex member as an induced subgraph yet has barely more than n vertices and edges. This cuts the earlier O(n^2) vertex bound and the O(n^(3/2)) edge bound. It is an existence result in theoretical computer science, with no claim about practical use.
title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes
